hot.title: Language Model Harnesses Can Be Compositional Generalizers
hot.summary: The paper trains a recursive language model harness to handle long tasks by keeping context outside the prompt, using code to inspect it, and delegating smaller queries to model calls. On eight held-out long-context benchmarks, RLM-27B averages 58.5 versus 46.1 for Qwen3.8-27B in the same harness; this is a benchmark-score gain, not a compute or time result.

hot.title: Counterfactual World Models: JEPAs That Reason About "What If"
hot.summary: The authors estimate what an alternative action would have done in the same event by adding the factual model’s predicted change between actions to the observed outcome. This reuses event-specific disturbance without paired counterfactual data or retraining. In simulated HandReach, physical counterfactual R-squared rises from 38.1% to 85.6% after physical readout correction; the result depends on structural conditions.

hot.title: A Society of AI Scientists
hot.summary: The authors study how agents develop research practices in a shared workspace, where 936 agents across 35 human-operated labs published studies and exchanged 9,500 messages over twelve weeks. Agents used public corrections, pre-run critique, and an agent-run journal. Executing reviewers’ major objections overturned 49.4% of tested headlines, but the observational deployment does not establish causation or independent scientific autonomy.

hot.title: A Claimed Proof of the Riemann Hypothesis
hot.summary: Levent Alpöge’s note describes a proposed route to the Riemann Hypothesis, using chained theta lifts to mimic multiplicity in Stepanov’s function-field method, which concerns a different setting. Alpöge reports Claude suggested a chain about √X long for a von Mangoldt sum of length X, and claims the approach extends to GRH; the note offers no readable proof or verification.

hot.title: Composable Soft-Prompt Distillation of RL Experts: Toward Continual Post-Training
hot.summary: CSPD addresses continual reinforcement-learning post-training by distilling each expert separately into a soft prompt while keeping the pre-training backbone frozen, then concatenating prompts at inference. This lets experts be added or removed without retraining shared weights. In a four-domain experiment, the combined prompts raised the average from 50.41 to 67.83, essentially matching MOPD’s 67.79; results are limited to this setup.

hot.title: The Content–Geometry Tradeoff in World Models: When JEPA Learns Latent Maps
hot.summary: Slow SVReg extends sliced variance regularization with slow channels and a gated predictor that defaults to copying the current representation. It aims to smooth latent routes while preserving slowly changing task-relevant content. In first-person PointMaze Medium hard-goal planning, it reaches 92.9 ± 3.2% versus 75.3 ± 5.5% for SVReg without those additions, across six models; these success rates apply to that setting.

hot.title: Feedback Shortcut: Speculative Decoding for Latent Feedback Transformers
hot.summary: Feedback Shortcut enables speculative decoding for latent-feedback Transformers. It aligns multi-token prediction head states as feedback stand-ins, then recomputes pending positions during the next verification call. For a 780M model with three heads, one correction, and batch size 1, it reports 0.8287 BPB versus 0.8288 for exact decoding, and 2.75× throughput; this is single-GPU steady-state serving, not exact output equivalence.

hot.title: Mind2Act World: A Diagnostic Benchmark for Embodied Mind, Physical Action, and Mind-Action Composition in Robotic Manipulation
hot.summary: Mind2Act World tests whether robots use memory, execution, and feedback across related simulated tabletop tasks. It separates memory-focused Mind tasks, action-focused Act tasks, and workflows where outcomes guide later decisions. GPT-6 Astra succeeds on 52.7% of Mind episodes, 39.0% of Act episodes, and 12.0% of Mind2Act episodes. These task-set rates do not isolate composition as the cause, and physical-robot transfer remains unmeasured.

hot.title: TideCache: Efficient Hybrid LLM Serving with Transparent Cache Management and Layer-Wise Streaming
hot.summary: TideCache serves hybrid models by dynamically reallocating GPU pages between global-KV and bounded-state caches while streaming historical prefixes from host memory layer by layer. It overlaps transfers with computation and keeps newly generated KV resident. On GPT-OSS-120B/GH200, it completes 2.04× as many agent turns as tuned SGLang with HiCache when prefixes exceed global-KV capacity, a serving result rather than less generation work.

hot.title: A CPU Inside an LLM: Zero-Gradient Compilation of Exact Circuits into Pretrained Weights
hot.summary: The authors graft a deterministic arithmetic circuit into pretrained model weights, enabling signed addition, subtraction, and multiplication without gradient updates, labeled examples, or runtime tool calls. Scale-robust circuit primitives and tokenizer-aligned emission let the language model resume after the answer. On Arith-1200, BF16 grafts reach 99.17% on Granite 4.2 3B and 100.00% on Qwen 3.5 4B, within the suite’s tested formats.

hot.title: Coda-DaVinci: Reimagining Video Generation with Code2Video
hot.summary: Coda-DaVinci uses selective executable 3D scene proxies to represent layout, interactions, and persistent state, while leaving appearance and fine motion to the video model. It uses coarse human proxies or direct generation when detailed control could constrain natural movement. On VTR-Bench, it scores 91.42 in checklist satisfaction and 11.08% WER, but does not lead every metric.

hot.title: Depth Pro 2: Sharp and Temporally Consistent Metric Monocular Depth
hot.summary: Depth Pro 2 estimates metric depth from images and video by processing frames jointly at native resolution with within-frame and cross-frame attention. In zero-shot comparisons, H+ ranks first for video metric-depth accuracy, boundary sharpness, and temporal consistency. On Sintel with predicted intrinsics, H+ reaches 41.4% δ1 versus 37.0% for UniDepthV2-L; rankings summarize separate measures, and results vary by model size.

hot.title: Frontier Models Need Only One Text to Unmask Its Human or AI Author
hot.summary: The authors test whether models can attribute single texts to human authors or AI labs without web access, tools, or candidate lists. Using zero-shot prompts, they assess prose, ideas, AI-source, and author attribution. Claude Fable 5.2 names authors of 56% of 398 private reviews, but these came from six writers, limiting what the score says about peer review generally.

hot.title: Posterior Matching Distillation
hot.summary: Posterior Matching Distillation (PMD) trains a stochastic few-step image generator to preserve multiple plausible clean images for the same noisy input. It matches exponentially weighted student predictions to shifted-input targets from a frozen teacher under Gaussian corruption. On four-step FLUX.2 [klein] 4B, PMD reaches Vendi 3.3708 versus 2.4104 for SMD, with FID 24.12 versus 24.58 for the base model.

hot.title: EgoCaptioner: Towards Comprehensive and Fine-Grained Egocentric Video Captioning
hot.summary: EgoCaptioner pairs video overview with timed, ordered steps whose detail adapts to activity type. It uses coarse-to-fine annotation to establish event structure before expanding step descriptions and trains captions with complementary rewards. In a matched comparison, it improves EgoTempo accuracy from 26.60% to 36.40% and EgoHome PSJ from 62.89 to 71.63; downstream assistant or robot performance is not demonstrated.

hot.title: On Evaluating User Simulators for Interactive Agents
hot.summary: The authors evaluate metrics for simulated users by testing whether scores detect controlled replay defects. They compare altered replays with controls from the same source session and agent assignment, using checks for agent rankings, population behavior, and fidelity to each user. Their suite detects all 10 designed perturbations, versus 5–6 for prior suites, under the tested protocols.

hot.title: MAWAM: A Multi-Agent World-Action Model for Coordinated Manipulation
hot.summary: Mawam coordinates robot teams by jointly predicting each robot’s next actions and future private camera views. A Transformer lets agents’ action and view predictions interact while keeping their inputs and controls distinct. On two Galaxea R1 Pro robots, Mawam averaged 67.8% success across three tasks, versus 48.9% for MA-VLA, in this fixed-team setup; it does not establish broader team support.

hot.title: Unified Law for Visual Tasks (The Four Laws of Computer Vision)
hot.summary: The authors propose World Snapshot Models, which treat visual tasks as directed condition-to-target mappings through task-specific routes in a shared, frozen image generator. For structured outputs, Modality Tunneling Attention produced structured RGB-to-normal output at 250 optimizer updates, versus 4,750 for a matched Native Joint Attention baseline. The study evaluates 1,148 dense mappings, not every visual task or world attribute.

hot.title: Piccolo: Co-Evolving Decision Models and Data through Recursive Self-Improvement
hot.summary: Piccolo develops decision models that return probabilities for supplied choices, rather than generating answer text. It reads logits for single-token candidate labels and uses semantic slices to guide human-steered data and training experiments. In the 17 November 2026 Decision Index Vision snapshot, Piccolo-27B scored 75.59, ahead of JDI-Decision V1 at 75.05, a benchmark result, not evidence of superiority or measured speedup.

hot.title: Grana: Compositional Reward Modeling for Long-Horizon Robot Manipulation
hot.summary: Grana estimates robot-task progress by selecting an unfinished subtask and predicting its local progress, then adding credit for preceding completed subtasks. Sparse boundary and action-quality annotations train its shared vision-language predictor to represent setbacks and recovery. On 50 held-out tasks, zero-shot RMSE was 0.180 versus 0.227 for fine-tuned RoboMeter, a 20.7% reduction, but this does not guarantee performance on arbitrary unseen tasks.

likes.title: $π^4$: A Foundation Model for 4D Scene Geometry and Motion
likes.summary: π⁴ reconstructs moving scenes from uncalibrated images or video, estimating geometry, camera poses, scale, and motion. It predicts image-space correspondences and lifts them onto reconstructed target-view geometry to place tracks in 3D. The paper reports the best overall average geometry rank (3.00) and competitive tracking results, but this rank does not establish superior metric-scale accuracy.

likes.title: ScaleVLA: Scaling Vision-Language-Action Models to 552 Billion Parameters
likes.summary: ScaleVLA connects a frozen 552-billion-parameter vision-language backbone to a trainable action head, which converts image, instruction, and robot-state features into action chunks without generating text. In fixed-budget benchmarks, it reaches 87.8% LIBERO-Goal success with 10 demonstrations per task, versus 85.6% for a 2B policy with 50. Its comparisons do not isolate parameter count from model-family differences.

likes.title: Weight-Space Programming Doesn’t Need Transformers
likes.summary: The paper studies WSP, where an LLM writes another model’s weights directly, without gradient training. The authors let LLMs choose model structures; three writers independently produce sparse fact tables. Claude Opus 5.5’s first-generation table reaches 50.8% ARC accuracy with 0.94 million parameters, about 1,800 times fewer than the 1.72-billion-parameter Qwen3-1.7B model written by that writer. The finding is limited to untrained models and multiple-choice recall.

likes.title: SLAM Dunk: A Recipe for Long-Horizon Egocentric SLAM in the Wild
likes.summary: SLAM Dunk improves offline visual–inertial bundle adjustment by allowing stereo-camera calibration to vary over time and fitting gyroscope scale and axis-misalignment errors. On the held-out LaMAria leaderboard, it exceeded Aria in three of five categories, including Medium (78.9 versus 78.5 CP), but its equally weighted category mean was lower (75.46 versus 75.86). This supports near-parity on the benchmark, not an overall win.

likes.title: The Resolution Hypothesis: Agent Evolution's Key Is Identifying Improvements
likes.summary: The paper examines whether noisy evaluations limit frozen-weight agent evolution. It measures both candidate quality and selectors’ ability to identify better artifacts, using skill pools and benchmark comparisons. On Terminal-Bench, a 100-skill pool exceeds an equal-quality null by 3.4 pp, while one-rollout selection is statistically indistinguishable from chance. The evidence concerns tested frozen-weight settings, not all self-improvement.

likes.title: Stream of Belief: Eliciting Collective Intelligence through Latent Belief Dynamics
likes.summary: Stream of Belief treats multi-agent reasoning as repeated exchange and revision of continuous internal beliefs. Agents alternate global interaction, using other agents’ beliefs, with local refinement based on their own belief and the problem; belief tokens mix embeddings from the top 50 candidate tokens. On GPQA-Diamond, SoB scores 44.9% versus LatentMAS’s 34.3%, below debate’s 53.0%.

likes.title: Latent Lattice Language Models
likes.summary: The authors introduce the Lattice, adding persistent per-layer states that recur across tokens alongside the Transformer’s vertical residual stream. These states condition attention and the MLP without adding token positions or KV-cache entries. After 20B FineWeb-Edu tokens, its 405.6M-parameter model reaches perplexity 14.40 versus 15.41 for a 406.7M baseline at approximately matched forward compute: 0.72 versus 0.71 GFLOP/token.

likes.title: K2-Horizon: A Frontier Fleet of Open Source Language Models
likes.summary: K2-Horizon releases six models with checkpoints, logs, training data, and code. The authors train four dense and sparse models on a shared 22-trillion-token corpus; their normalized loss curves nearly overlap, though normalization aligns endpoints. At final mid-training, 36B-A4B scores 86.9 on 0-shot MMLU versus 88.1 for dense 32B, with about one-seventh as many active backbone parameters per token.

likes.title: NVIDIA Kumo Tabular: Pushing the Accuracy–Efficiency Frontier for Tabular Prediction
likes.summary: Kumo Tabular predicts labels from labeled rows using a pretrained encoder and transformer, without task-specific weight updates or hyperparameter search. Its encoder alternates column and row attention before compressing rows for in-context prediction. Kumo Tabular-L ranks first on primary metrics across eight benchmarks, but Elo intervals overlap top non-Kumo results, and performance is weaker on grouped splits and tables above 100K training rows.

likes.title: Do LLM Agents Still Need to Be Told How to Self-Improve?
likes.summary: The authors test whether language models can design their own learning procedures for puzzle play, using a frozen teacher to create games, observe a player, and revise its text context. Newer models improve on held-out PuzzleScript-t20, with Claude Opus 5 gaining +20%, and its context transfers to longer PuzzleScript, ARC-AGI-3, and MazeBench. The evidence is limited to puzzle settings.

likes.title: ALOHA Lightning: Learning Fast and Precise Manipulation
likes.summary: ALOHA Lightning speeds robot manipulation by collecting demonstrations through direct, hands-on guidance of the robot arms and adapting learned policies for autonomous execution. It blends overlapping action chunks to smooth motion and masks operator regions in training and deployment images. On battery insertion, it achieves 85% whole-task success in 5.70 seconds; toss-and-catch takes 1.85 seconds with 50% success.

likes.title: Decoding Without a Decoder: Direct Pixel Prediction from Diffusion Transformers
likes.summary: DWD removes the decoder from latent diffusion generation by adding a linear pixel-prediction head alongside the denoising head. The original head continues to guide sampling, while the pixel head predicts pixels at the final step. It reduces Wan2.1 14B video warping error from 1.52 to 1.18 × 10⁻³ and AnisoFlow-H/16 FID from 1.55 to 1.43 in the tested settings.

likes.title: M3OPD-Reasoner: An Open Recipe for Post-Training Multimodal Reasoning with Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation
likes.summary: The authors train a vision-language model across image science and math, perception, and video by training domain specialists, distilling their guidance into a shared student on its own responses, then applying reward-based reinforcement learning. Across 21 benchmarks, it scores 75.2 avg@8 versus 74.4 for direct mixed training; the added reinforcement-learning stage raises it to 75.9, within this evaluation setup.
